mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) increases the cost of capital and compresses equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is negative, so the hypothesis predicts negative returns when FEDFUNDS is elevated.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (as of t-1mo).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1600) signals weakening consumer demand and reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The threshold captures significant downturns in residential construction.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1600, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 202.0) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0) signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing corporate profit growth and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 202.0 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.5%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, when UNRATE > 4.5%, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low level of industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) indicates weakening manufacturing activity and reduced economic output, lowering corporate profit expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is negative.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110.0, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP growth (GDPC1 < 11500) reflects slowing economic expansion, reducing corporate earnings growth and equity demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The threshold captures significant GDP weakness.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 < 11500, the 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 202.0) combined with elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0) creates a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 202.0 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0, the 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS < 137000) signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, when PAYEMS < 137000, the 5-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
